label: M. pneumoniae
plain: A small bacterium of the human airways, among the smallest organisms that copy themselves: 688 proteins in the genome record frozen here, in a thin cell about 2 µm long with one membrane, no wall and an attachment organelle at one end.

modelled.text: Its public measurements were audited beside the minimal-cell track on JCVI-syn3A (decision D173; the track's note of 15 November 2026), which recommends it to lead a later stage on energy, transport and pH. Nothing of it is in the engine, and no model of it has run.

record.where: D173: M. pneumoniae is audited soon
9.3 Should M. pneumoniae lead a stage?

levels.label: One cell
levels.note: Drawn as a rod 2 µm long and 0.2 µm across, the upper ends of the ranges given for the cell, with 300 ribosomes. The real cell is not a plain rod: it changes shape, and one end narrows into the attachment organelle, about 0.3 µm long, which this shape cannot show.

no_further_levels: A single-celled organism: each cell lives on its own, on the cells of its host, so it has no tissue, organ or body of its own.

facts.label: Shape and size
facts.value: a thin cell 1 to 2 µm long and 0.1 to 0.2 µm wide, of changeable shape, drawn out at one end into its attachment organelle; one paper gives its volume as 0.075 µm³

facts.label: Attachment organelle
facts.value: a membrane protrusion at one pole, 250 to 300 nm long, with an internal core; it carries the adhesins and leads the cell when it glides

facts.label: Envelope
facts.value: a cell membrane stiffened by sterols, and no cell wall; UniProt's curated entries of its proteins name one membrane, the cell membrane, and no outer one

facts.label: Inside
facts.value: a small prokaryote, among the smallest organisms that copy themselves: a bacterium, with no nucleus

facts.label: Genes
facts.value: 688 protein products in the genome record frozen here, the re-annotation of 2000; a review counts 687 genes, a re-annotation of 2015 has 694 reading frames, and UniProt has 686 entries

facts.label: Ribosomes
facts.value: about 300 in a cell: the proteins of the ribosome were measured at a median of 300 copies in a cell, by mass spectrometry

facts.label: Proteins
facts.value: about 120,000 protein molecules in a cell, the sum over 528 kinds of protein measured by mass spectrometry, three quarters of all its kinds

facts.label: Doubling time
facts.value: about 8 hours in rich medium; 17.6 hours were measured in a serum-free medium

facts.label: Essential genes
facts.value: 342 of 694 genes essential, 93 needed for normal growth and 259 dispensable, by transposon mutagenesis

facts.label: Energy
facts.value: ATP from fermenting glucose, with lactate and acetate as end products; mycoplasmas lack the citric acid cycle

facts.label: Food
facts.value: glucose as its main fuel; it makes almost none of its own building blocks, no amino acids, vitamins or lipids among them, and takes them up

facts.label: Ion channels
facts.value: none found among its 688 proteins; one glycerol facilitator of the aquaporin family

facts.label: Division
facts.value: in two, by binary fission; the attachment organelle is duplicated first and takes part in the division

facts.label: Movement
facts.value: glides on surfaces, attachment organelle first, at up to 1 µm a second

facts.label: Name
facts.value: databases now list it as Mycoplasmoides pneumoniae; the papers cited call it Mycoplasma pneumoniae

cap.membrane.note: Its one membrane holds the cell's ion and proton gradients. In a model of its metabolism published in 2020 the ATP synthase runs in reverse and pumps protons out of the cell; that is the model's result, and no source read for this file measured the voltage.

cap.channels.why: No ion channel was found among its 688 proteins: none carries the signature of a channel family in Cells' catalogue, or of the bacterial channels for potassium, chloride, magnesium or membrane stretch, which the same search does find in other mollicutes. One protein, the glycerol facilitator GlpF, carries the signature of the family of water and glycerol channels; it is not an ion channel.

cap.pumps.note: Not the pumps of animal cells: it has no sodium-potassium pump. By its annotation, its ATP-driven ion movers are the ATP synthase, one P-type ATPase whose ion is not known, and a potassium uptake system.

cap.junctions.why: It lives as single cells and has no gap junctions: none of its proteins carries the signature of connexins or innexins.

cap.extracellular.note: Here it is what surrounds the single cell: the surface of the airway cells it lives on, or a growth medium. The cell depends on it: it makes no amino acids, vitamins or lipids of its own and takes them up.

cap.water.note: It has no cell wall: nothing but the membrane bounds its volume. One of its proteins, GlpF, belongs to the family of water and glycerol channels.

cap.calcium.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum: it is a bacterium with a single membrane and no internal compartments, and none of its proteins carries the signature of the store's calcium pump or of its release channels.

cap.energy.note: Its ATP comes from fermenting sugar in the cytoplasm, with lactate and acetate as end products; mycoplasmas lack the citric acid cycle.

cap.mitochondria.why: It is a bacterium and has no mitochondria. Its ATP synthase sits in the cell membrane.

cap.circuits.note: At the chromosome, which lies in the cytoplasm: there is no nucleus.

cap.grn.why: It forms no tissue, so there is nothing for gene networks to be coupled across. Gene expression within the one cell belongs with regulatory circuits.

cap.trafficking.why: It has no endoplasmic reticulum and no Golgi. By its annotation, new membrane proteins are put straight into the cell membrane by the Sec translocon and the YidC insertase.

cap.assembly.note: Its assemblies are its ribosomes, RNA polymerase, the ATP synthase and the internal core of its attachment organelle. The designed protein cage that Cells models is not one of its proteins.

cap.machines.note: About 300 ribosomes, with RNA polymerase, the ATP synthase, the protein translocon and the machinery in its attachment organelle that lets it glide. None of its proteins carries the proteasome's signature; its annotation lists the proteases FtsH and Lon.

cap.secretion.note: It releases lactate and acetate, the end products of its fermentation, and takes its nutrients up. Signalling between its own cells was not looked for.

cap.repair.note: The place would be its bare membrane. No source read for this file describes a membrane injury or its resealing in this organism.

cap.division.note: It divides in two as a single cell. Its attachment organelle is duplicated first and takes part in the division; the division gene ftsZ is in its genome.

cap.replacement.why: It forms no tissue, so there is no neighbour for a new cell to replace.

cap.mechanics.why: It forms no sheet: its cells share no edges to pull on. Its own movement, gliding on a surface, is not what this capability models.

cap.sheet.why: It lives as single cells and forms no sheet of coupled cells.
